When may sync start?

For a local home NAS, an IP address list matching your home network is a practical restriction. This is not a secure way to identify a Wi-Fi network: other networks can use the same address range. Leave public IP addresses disabled unless necessary.
No Wi-Fi connection is required. Sync can be attempted over other networks, subject to the public-IP restriction below.
Requires an active Wi-Fi connection, but accepts any Wi-Fi network. It does not verify that you are at home.
Requires a private IPv4 address (10.x.x.x, 172.16–31.x.x or 192.168.x.x). This could be a different network or VPN, not necessarily home Wi-Fi.
Compares an IP address found on this phone against your allowed list. Add the phone\'s home IP or a pattern such as 192.168.1.*. Do not enter the NAS IP unless it is also the phone\'s IP.
Which IP address belongs in the list?

Enter your PHONE\'s private IP address on the home network, or its subnet with a wildcard (example: 192.168.1.*). Not the NAS address. Find the phone address in Android Wi-Fi details. Another network can reuse the same range, and VPN or other interfaces may affect which IP the legacy app detects.
Skip instead of reporting an error
If your phone\'s IP address does not match the list, mark this task as skipped instead of treating it as a sync error. Useful when the task is scheduled and you are away from home.
Allow public IP addresses
Allows the task to start even when the phone\'s detected address is public. This does not grant NAS permissions or configure remote access. Leave disabled for normal backups to a NAS at home.
Incremental photo backup
Copy only since newest file on destination
Also copy changes to older files already on destination
How incremental copy works

For Copy tasks from internal phone storage to an SMB folder only. Before copying, the app finds the most recently modified file on the target (including subfolders). It skips source files whose original photo date is older; it uses the filename timestamp or file modification time when an original photo date is unavailable. If older-file changes are enabled, it also checks older files that already exist on the destination and copies them when different, without backfilling missing older files. The first backup to an empty folder is a full copy. WARNING: changing the time of an old destination file can move the cutoff forward, and photos with missing/incorrect date metadata can be skipped. This is an optional speed optimization, not a complete backup strategy.
Incremental copy currently supports only Copy tasks from internal Android storage to an SMB folder, without date-based target folder renaming. Disable the option for this task.
